html:
Gediminas was Grand Duke of Lithuania from about 1316 to 1341. He made Lithuania a great power in eastern Europe and Vilnius its capital.

In letters of 1323 to German towns he invited merchants, craftsmen and monks to settle in his lands, promising freedom of faith. These letters are the first written mention of Vilnius. By legend he founded the city after dreaming of an iron wolf howling on a hill.

He held off the Teutonic Knights and pushed east into the lands of the old Kievan Rus, ruling many Orthodox subjects while himself staying pagan. His descendants, the Gediminids, included Jogaila and Vytautas and ruled Poland and Lithuania for centuries. See Lithuania.
sum: Gediminas was Grand Duke of Lithuania from about 1316 to 1341. He made Lithuania a great power in eastern Europe and Vilnius its capital.
